faq: Is the provider's own portal good enough?
For many small products, yes. It is quick, secure and maintained for you. A custom page is better when you want your own design or extra steps, such as a cancel survey.
Can customers see invoices from before this was built?
Yes, if those invoices were created in the same provider account. Older invoices from another tool can be linked or listed, but we confirm that first.
Does the portal work for team accounts?
It can, if your app already has teams. We decide who may see billing, usually owners only. Team and role features themselves are covered by our user accounts services.
Is card data safe on the page?
Card details are entered in the provider's secure fields and never pass through your server. We do not see or store them at any point.

desc:
A customer billing portal for SaaS subscribers, built by Ecom Swift LLC. It gives customers one self-service page to switch plans, update a card, check the next payment and download invoices, so simple billing questions stop reaching your inbox.

## What is a customer billing portal?

A customer billing portal is a page inside your app where subscribers manage their own payments. They can see the current plan, change it, replace an expired card, read past invoices and cancel. Behind the page, it talks to your payment provider, so the information is always the live record and never a copy someone typed in.

There are two routes. Many providers offer a ready-made portal that you switch on and style. The other route is a billing page built in your own design that calls the provider securely and shows only the actions you want. Both are valid, and the right choice depends on how much control and brand consistency you need.

## Why self-service billing saves time and keeps customers

Look at the support inbox of almost any subscription product and you will find the same messages: please send me last month's invoice, my card changed, how do I switch to the yearly plan, how do I cancel. Each one is simple, yet each needs a person to read it, check the account and reply. Multiplied across a growing customer list, this becomes a steady drain on a small team.

A portal removes that queue. It also improves retention in a quieter way. A customer who can update a card in a minute does not lapse by accident, and a customer who can see their plan and next payment date trusts the product more. If cancelling is easy and honest, you also get a chance to ask why, which is useful information for the roadmap.

## What a good billing portal includes

- Current plan name, price and billing period, shown at the top.
- The next payment date and amount.
- Card update through the provider's secure form, so card data never touches your server.
- A list of past invoices with PDF downloads.
- Plan switching, with a price preview before the customer confirms.
- Cancellation at the end of the paid period, with an optional reason question.
- Billing email and company details that appear on invoices.
- Confirmation emails after each change.
- Your logo and colors, so the page matches the rest of the product.
- Pause or reactivate options, where your plans allow them.

## How we build it

We begin by checking how customers are stored in your provider and in your app, because the portal must find the right billing record for each logged-in user. The Basic package turns on the provider's portal, enables cards, invoices and cancellation, applies your branding and adds an Open portal button in your app. The Standard package builds a billing page in your own design with the plan, next payment, card update, invoice list and cancel flow. The Premium package adds plan switching with a price preview, company details, pause or cancel at period end, confirmation emails and a handover call.

Security is part of the job. The portal only ever shows the billing record that belongs to the logged-in customer, and card entry happens inside the provider's own secure form. We test with several accounts to confirm that one customer cannot see another's invoices.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Put a clear Billing link in the account menu where customers expect it.
- Show the next payment date and amount without any clicking.
- Let customers download invoices as PDFs at any time.
- Confirm every change by email.
- Ask a short, optional question when someone cancels.

**Avoid:**
- Hiding the cancel option behind several screens.
- Building your own card form when the provider offers a secure one.
- Allowing plan changes without showing the new price first.
- Sending customers to a portal that looks nothing like your product.
- Showing billing details to anyone other than the account owner or billing contact.

## Who this suits

This service suits a SaaS founder who answers the same billing emails every week. It suits a product with team accounts that needs a billing contact separate from regular users. It also suits a company that launched with the provider's default portal and now wants a page that feels like part of its own app.

## What we need from you

Tell us which payment provider you use and how your users log in. Share your logo and colors, and tell us which actions you want customers to take on their own. For access, a developer or collaborator seat in your app's code and a team role in your provider account are enough, and passwords are never part of the process. After ordering, you receive a short checklist and a preview link before the portal goes live.
